review_1: I've been using the Logitech MK955 for a few months and it's quickly become my favorite keyboard/mouse combo. The full‑size keyboard has a generous layout that fits my larger hands, and the keys are whisper‑quiet but still have a satisfying feel. The ergonomic mouse is equally comfortable and tracks smoothly on various surfaces. I love that I can switch between my desktop, laptop and tablet with a single button thanks to the multi‑device Bluetooth pairing. Setup was simple and it works flawlessly on both Windows and Mac. Battery life has been excellent and the build quality feels premium. If you need a reliable wireless keyboard and mouse with quiet typing and seamless device switching, this set is worth the investment.
review_2: This keyboard is perfect and exactly what I needed. I wanted a higher quality wireless keyboard for work and this one is that plus some. Keys are not too loud but also not silent. If you’re on the fence due to the price, just purchase and know you’ll never have to buy another keyboard again.

review_1: I type all day for work, fast, about 125wpm on a bad day. I use lots of hot keys, tab switching and window jumping. This has a good "clack" to the keys for such a long profile. The mouse is a good enough resolution for basic games and graphic design, and feels solid with a fast bootup. Smooth install on Windows 10 laptop took only a few seconds, just put in batteries, turn on the mouse, which governs power on the keyboard via a bonded connection (more on this later) and the keyboard doesn't have a dedicated power switch itself. After that just plug in the wireless USB dongle / adapter and the rest of the install is automatic and very fast. Don't be silly and expect to use this stuff for competitive gaming, it's wireless and on normal batteries.Two points to remember:The keyboard is coded at the factory to the specific mouse that's in the box. Great for easy setup and security, but IF YOU LOSE THERE MOUSE THE KEYBOARD IS USELESS. There is no realistic way around this.Second- the Escape key is a tiny hard to find thing and will mock you as you search for it in your angriest of moments. Fear not, the mouse still works fine after you put the keyboard on the garbage disposal. (but the keyboard is not replaceable, soooo you would do well to see if someone only needs a mouse and start from scratch after giving the mouse to someone in need) Read more

review_1: I broke a key on my laptop and needed a replacement keyboard, as well as a mouse (since it's really inconvenient to reach over a keyboard to use the touchpad on my laptop). I have my laptop propped up on a stand and the entire setup just works beautifully.Pros:- The mouse and keyboard connected right away through a single USB.- I don't think the keyboard was charged all the way when it came, so it ran out after a few days but it was really simple to charge and it's working great.- the keyboard is slightly smaller than what I'm used to, but I adjust quickly :) I love how the enter and backspace keys are well sized, and how there's no number pad hanging along on the right.- keyboard shortcuts work for me, including copy/paste/cut as well as the keyboard shortcuts for changing language input.- The sound of the keyboard is clickier than I was anticipating (definitely not what I would call quiet), but it's not disruptive and I've gotten used to it.- It's very thin and light! I crocheted a sleeve for it so that I can transport it without worrying about dropping it.Considerations:- I have to click the mouse once to wake it from sleep before I can use it.- Like some people suggested in other reviews, I went and toggled my computer for mouse speed / scrolling speed so it's at a level that I'm satisfied with.- the mouse looks very modern and is ergonomic, feeling great under the hand!If something happens to this product I will come back here to let y'all know, but I am very satisfied thus far :)EDIT: I just charged the mouse for the first time since when I bought it in June! That's a very very long battery life like other reviews told me and I'm quite pleased with it! Read more
review_2: I just received it and am using it to type this review. Before this, I've been using the wireless logitech full sized keyboard, but decided to buy this because I needed more space on my desk.First Impressions: Good buy! The receiver for the keyboard and mouse plugs and just works. No hassle at all. I don't know if it will be the case for everyone else, but I didn't need to charge/plug it in straight from the box. We'll see how long it lasts.The keys aren't all that silent, but it doesn't bother me since I'm used to that anyway. They're good keys, if you're not used to something hellishly expensive. If you're expecting the keys to be as quiet as, say the ones on the Macbook Pro (2015)⁠—that's not what you'll be getting. Another thing I noticed was that the Windows shortcut (alt+0151) for the em dash just doesn't work. Ctrl+alt+delete DOES work, I should mention while I'm on this topic. I'm not too sure what else does and doesn't work aside from that since I don't really use shortcuts. It's not a deal breaker for me, but I thought I should mention it. There's no lag or out of control keys. It types as fast as I do, stops when I do, and generally works great.The mouse...hmm. Well, I'll say it feels nice and is of good build quality for the price point. It doesn't feel all that plastic-y and too light like some other mice I've tried. I like the way it feels and I like how quiet it is and I like how easily the wheel in the middle scrolls. Though I did right-click things by accident a few times, that was because it was more sensitive than I was used to and I adjusted pretty quickly. That being said, I've put it away in favor of another mouse I already own⁠. The shape is just too flat for my wrist to be comfortable. Since I am on the computer for long periods of time, that matters a lot to me. It is a nicely built mouse⁠—just not for me.I do a lot of creative work, so I opened Photoshop to check the basic shortcuts. The shortcuts for brushes, pen, eraser, type, and all the other tools work fine. Resizing brushes via the bracket keys works! Ctrl+Z works fine. Ctrl+Shift+N works fine. Ctrl+F, which I've chained to flipping the canvas horizontally, also works fine. Ctrl+Shift+S also works great! Haven't checked for more than that, but I suspect it'll also work just fine. Don't know how it works with other programs/apps, but I'm pretty happy since this is all I need and all I checked for.What else? I like the size and look of the keyboard. It's even more compact than I expected, which is good, but also big enough that my fingers are NOT accidentally hitting the wrong keys. I also like the stainless back of the keyboard⁠—makes it feel more solid and heavier than a pure plastic keyboard while also still being very light. I'm picky about how my stuff feels, so this was one of the deciding factors for me in getting this keyboard, along with the good connectivity/working reviews. Read more

review_2: I just received it and am using it to type this review. Before this, I've been using the wireless logitech full sized keyboard, but decided to buy this because I needed more space on my desk.First Impressions: Good buy! The receiver for the keyboard and mouse plugs and just works. No hassle at all. I don't know if it will be the case for everyone else, but I didn't need to charge/plug it in straight from the box. We'll see how long it lasts.The keys aren't all that silent, but it doesn't bother me since I'm used to that anyway. They're good keys, if you're not used to something hellishly expensive. If you're expecting the keys to be as quiet as, say the ones on the Macbook Pro (2015)⁠—that's not what you'll be getting. Another thing I noticed was that the Windows shortcut (alt+0151) for the em dash just doesn't work. Ctrl+alt+delete DOES work, I should mention while I'm on this topic. I'm not too sure what else does and doesn't work aside from that since I don't really use shortcuts. It's not a deal breaker for me, but I thought I should mention it. There's no lag or out of control keys. It types as fast as I do, stops when I do, and generally works great.The mouse...hmm. Well, I'll say it feels nice and is of good build quality for the price point. It doesn't feel all that plastic-y and too light like some other mice I've tried. I like the way it feels and I like how quiet it is and I like how easily the wheel in the middle scrolls. Though I did right-click things by accident a few times, that was because it was more sensitive than I was used to and I adjusted pretty quickly. That being said, I've put it away in favor of another mouse I already own⁠. The shape is just too flat for my wrist to be comfortable. Since I am on the computer for long periods of time, that matters a lot to me. It is a nicely built mouse⁠—just not for me.I do a lot of creative work, so I opened Photoshop to check the basic shortcuts. The shortcuts for brushes, pen, eraser, type, and all the other tools work fine. Resizing brushes via the bracket keys works! Ctrl+Z works fine. Ctrl+Shift+N works fine. Ctrl+F, which I've chained to flipping the canvas horizontally, also works fine. Ctrl+Shift+S also works great! Haven't checked for more than that, but I suspect it'll also work just fine. Don't know how it works with other programs/apps, but I'm pretty happy since this is all I need and all I checked for.What else? I like the size and look of the keyboard. It's even more compact than I expected, which is good, but also big enough that my fingers are NOT accidentally hitting the wrong keys. I also like the stainless back of the keyboard⁠—makes it feel more solid and heavier than a pure plastic keyboard while also still being very light. I'm picky about how my stuff feels, so this was one of the deciding factors for me in getting this keyboard, along with the good connectivity/working reviews. Read more

review_1: I purchased the MK710 Keyboard/Mouse combo mainly to replace the HP wireless keyboard/mouse that I got with my desktop computer. I've had great experiences with Logitech products in the past, so I expected a high-quality product, and they did not disappoint! While I've only used it for a few hours so far, I am definitely happy with my purchase.Marathon mouse:This is a full-sized yet portable mouse that's specifically designed to be used with the right hand. It's very comfortable to use for long periods of time. I work from home, and am switching the receiver between my laptop during work hours and desktop during off hours, so I'll be using this mouse for easily 10 hours a day, sometimes more -- I feel like this mouse is ready for that!This is the first time I've had a mouse with extra buttons. There are three buttons on the right side: two obvious buttons near the top that are set to forward and back, and a button toward the bottom of the mouse. With the included software, you can completely customize the buttons to do whatever you'd like.I'm also a huge fan of the scroll wheel. You can quickly switch between "normal" scrolling and hyperscrolling for longer documents. It also can be held side-to-side to scroll left/right on things like spreadsheets where you have a lot of columns. VERY useful. I'd read some complaints about it not working well as a "normal" scroll wheel but I haven't found that to be the case. When it's engaged in normal mode, it acts just like any other scroll wheel I've used.The included software currently says I have over 900 days remaining on my mouse batteries. That's incredible!Keyboard:I'm impressed at how quiet the keys are. They are also rounded to feel more comfortable for long periods of typing. The markings on the F and J keys seem to stick up a bit more than on other keyboards I've used, but I don't find it bothersome at all. It took me a few minutes to feel comfortable with the feel of the keys and their response when typing, but I adjusted pretty quickly.The cushion below the main keyboard area is actually a cushion with a little squish to it. I expected hard plastic, so that's a nice touch. Also, if you're into putting an incline on your keyboard, there are actually two sets of legs, allowing you to choose between a 4 degree and 8 degree angle. I personally keep my keyboard flat to minimize carpal tunnel, but this could be useful to those who want to get that angle just right when typing.For the most part the function keys worked pretty well out of the box, but I used the included software to make some quick customizations. I also switched it so that you only hold the FN key when you want to use one of the F commands, so the quick-launch options are even easier to use.It's a silly feature, but I really like having the calculator key. I can't tell you how many times I pull up the calculator program during the day! And its location by the number pad makes perfect sense.I think my only complaint is that the length of the keyboard, once you include the wrist rest and the top section with LCD, is definitely bigger than I'm used to. I typically store the keyboard under my monitor when not in use, and it sticks out more than I'd like. But the keyboard is still very thin, and easy enough to tuck out of the way.Overall, I'm really pleased with this set. My old HP set used to have receiver issues, but this combo works flawlessly. Definitely worth the price, especially if you spend a lot of time at your computer. Read more
review_2: Superb keyboard and mouse - best I have had in 30 years' using PCs at home and work.I bought the Logitech MK710 wireless keyboard and mouse because I wanted a keyboard display of caps/number/scroll lock settings, something difficult to find especially in a wireless set. So many times I've had to rewrite passages and passwords and been frustrated with numbers not working and odd scrolling behavior because these settings had been mistakenly changed. A glance at the keyboard display helps avoid those problems. Happily, not only did I get an up-front, easy to read display, but an excellent keyboard and mouse - and wireless to boot!Keyboard: Tactile feel of the keys and palm wrest is great. Just the right amount of friction to let your hands and fingers slide around without being slippery. Keypress is perfect for me, too, taking a positive action, helping to avoid typos, but too hard and not too long. Key action is fairly silent, with just enough audible feedback. Text entry follows each keypress quickly and reliably. Function keys are nicely arranged at the top, easy to find, but not too large. Each function key also has a handy shortcut option, for example Fn-F1 opens browser homepage, Fn-F2 = email, Fn-F7 = zoom, Fn-F9 = music, etc. Additionally, there are separate buttons to control sound level, disc/file player operation (play/pause etc.), eject disk, and start calculator. Keyboard angle can be adjusted among three settings by opening/closing feet under keyboard. I find little to fault. Personally, I would like a palm rest that was a little wider, but my hands are large and fingers extra-long. I suspect the palm rest would be just fine for normal hands.Mouse: This is the M705 mouse. It has left and right buttons; dual-mode (see below) scroll wheel with horizontal as well as vertical scrolling plus middle-button functionality; forward and back buttons; and a trick application switch. Scroll wheel mode can be changed easily between smooth, fast free-wheel scrolling and fine-control click-stop scrolling by simply pressing a button on top of the mouse; very nice. Forward/back buttons are nicely positioned by the thumb (IF you are right-handed), are nicely sized to be out of the way until you want to use them, and take a positive but not-too-hard action to press. The application switcher works by pressing the thumb rest (again, for right-handed folks only) which causes your open applications to display as windows arrayed across the screen - simply point and click on the application you want; sweet. I find the mouse reasonably comfortable to use, though I would like one a bit larger - again, the large hand / long fingers thing. Wouldn't it be nice if you could get a mouse in small/medium/large sizes, and shaped for lefties as well as righties? Straight out of the box, the pointer movement was a bit faster than I prefer, but that is adjustable to your taste in the Logitech Setpoint software that comes with the mouse. After a few minutes, I was able to adjust pointer speed and acceleration to my personal preference.By now you probably think I have a personal connection with Logitech. Let me assure you, I do not. I just think this is a terrific keyboard/mouse combo with excellent quality at a reasonable price. Read more

review_2: I got the keyboard this morning, and it is a total joy. I have to say, it's likely the best 'non-gaming' keyboard I have ever used. Layout is phenomenal. Build quality is top notch, and they keys are sublime. The top is a solid piece of metal, and the back is plastic. I really dont mind the plastic, and it likely keeps the weight down a bit.For full disclosure, I would give it 4.5 stars if I had the option. The only thing I would like would be a full backlight, but thats far from a prerequisite if you are using it in a true office setting. There are LEDs under the num lock and caps lock button, and I am more than ok with that, given the $80 price tag for a very good keyboard and mouse combo.Which reminds me, the mouse is pretty darn good too. To be honest, I thought I would be sticking with my ole faithful that I had been using for the last 1.5 years, and using the Dell Premiere mouse as a backup, but that has already changed. the mouse has solid ergonomics, and functions for what appears to be a very minimalist device. The mouse even has a magnetic closure, and magnetized wireless dongle storage. Very nice touch for those that may be concerned about breaking the plastic clips over time, or somebody that may be frequently storing the wireless dongle for transport. the anti-friction pads on the back are also very good. These always wear down with time, but it is fairing better than any other mouse I have used on my textured desk surface. Nobody should have any qualms with the scroll wheel either.My only two gripes with the mouse were the cursor speed, and the fwd/back button locations. The cursor speed can be adjusted on almost any computer in settings, so its not a big deal. just know that out of the box, this thing is probably gonna zip around your screen at mach speed. In terms of the side buttons, the layout isnt exactly ideal. The back button is fine, but I would prefer that the fwd button on the right hand side either be a bit higher or stacked on top of the back button. e.g. have both of them on the left hand side. Of course, I know this was probably done to make the mouse fully ambidextrous, but its not ideal for the 90% of us that are righties. Read more

review_1:
Wow, this keyboard is smooth and quiet!

It's a replacement for a cheaper Logitech keyboard (MK200) and wanted to see how well the Amazon Basics holds up. Sure enough, I'm impressed! They keyboard is quiet, typing is smooth. The clicking on the mouse is silent! Sounds like a light 'thud' when using it. Same for the scroll wheel, nice and quiet!

It feels nice in my hands and it's nearly flat on my desk. No lag at all since it's a wired connection (something I get often from Logitech keyboards prior) and it's super easy to use! Just plug and play right out of the box! Functionality is a plus with buttons dedicated to the File Explorer (button with monitor icon) and Media Player (button with music note icon.)

Overall, it serves my needs perfectly. 5 stars across the board for the price!
review_2:
Excellent keyboard, totally recommend it for my Macbook Pro, and here's why...

So I spilled some coffee (just a little) on my Macbook Pro keyboard and the Command key died... its an older computer so I decided I'm just gonna let it be broken and get a replacement keyboard to use (and yes, I have learned my lesson!).

Tried a couple of $20-30 bluetooth keyboards by 2 different makers, both purchased on Amazon, and both suck for different reasons. In my research I found Amazon Basics, their line of products that they, as no surprise, closely monitor reviews and ratings on Amazon.com and make product improvements based on those reviews. And the 3 Amazon Basics products I've used so far have all been superior quality to all other unknown brands.

I just love this keyboard! Its well made, the keys feel great and it looks good (high gloss black body, matte black keys). Comes with a mouse too, which I though I just throw out, but I tried it out and to be honest after using an Apple trackpad for a few years, its a joy to use a mouse again :). The mouse is nice too, matte black, very light weight, simple.

It's a Windows keyboard, so you'll have to re-map the command key and options keys, just use an app like Karabiner, 5 min fix.

The only minor gripe I have with the keyboard is there's no Windows/alt/control key mirror to the right of the keyboard, instead there's a alt, right-click glyph tagged button, function key and control key (in that order). That strange right-click key is not recognized by Mac, so it can't be remapped with the app I'm using. So be warned if you must have an identical set up as a mac keyboard on the right, it ain't gonna happen. Even still...

For the price to quality ratio, definitely 5 stars.

It would be great to have a Mac version of this keyboard, so Amazon if you're listening, you've got my vote to make one :)

review_2: For reference my hand 18 cm measured from the first crease after your palm to the end of my middle finger. I flexed my wrist and the first crease I used as my end point for my palm. My arms are at a 90 degree angle, and my wrist is neutral (not flexed up or down) due to my wrist rest keeping my wrist straight. Most of my arm weight is on my memory foam wrist rest. My review is based on my personal hand sizeUpdate: After a month I have not noticed any staining on my white lift. But I am also a pretty hygienic person and I never touch my mouse if I touched food.Wrist pain:This might be because I don't have arm rests so the weight of my arm is resting on the wrist wrest, but I had some minor wrist pains within an hour or so. It didn't really feel like a muscle or bone kind of pain, but a nerve/soft tissue pain. When I didn't use a wrist rest, the weight was mostly the side of my hand, in particular the bony part near the wrist. That part rubbed when moving the mouse around if you don't lift your arm.Edit: After some adjustment I no longer get any wrist pain, even when gaming.Palm grip:I think palm grip would be unusable for this mouse. My fingers extend 0.5-1 cm after the end of the mouse (where the left and right buttons start curving). When clicking the mouse it almost feels like im clicking with my finger joint instead of my fingertip. With a relaxed thumb (thumb slightly curved and only fingertip touching mouse) it is pretty easy to click the side buttons. Side of thumb can press upper button, thumb joint can press lower button. With the entire thumb fully in contact with the mouse, the upper button is a bit awkward to press but possible, and the lower button is the same as relaxed thumb position. Awkward to use the scroll wheel since you have to curve your fingers quite a bit to get your finger tip on the scroll wheel but still usable. Also because of the hand angle, I found it much more comfortable using my middle finger to use the scroll wheel instead of my pointer finger that I use normally.Fingertip grip:Personally I found it feeling different, but perfect. My finger length is perfect so my fingers land around or slightly below where the left and right mouse button start to curve. When I click, the direction of the force from my finger is more diagonally down and to the left. If my fingers were a bit shorter, it the force would be to the left. I found this diagonally force feels more natural, kind of like squeezing a trigger (kinda) instead of just squeezing a mouse. It is hard to describe. In this grip, the only part of my fingers (including my thumb) that are touching the mouse are my fingertips. My palm is resting on the mouse. Thumb characteristics is same as palm grip. Scroll wheel characteristics same as palm grim.Claw grip:Works fine, only problem is pushing lower thumb button is a bit awkward since you kind have to shift your entire thumb back but it is still possible. Easy to use scroll wheel since your fingertips end right next to itCompared to g305:The Lift is much more comfortable and natural. I got used to the Lift very quickly. In comparison, the g305 felt like a petite mouse. The g305 felt hollow, like there was nothing supporting my palm. I didn't have any issues with the mouse shifting when clicking it on my mouse pad. Even on a smooth surface with no mouse pad it would happen rarely.Scroll wheel:Excellent combination of a normal scroll wheel and a free one. I can scroll down all the way to the end of reddit threads and spotify playlists in one scroll. Going back up takes a few scrolls however since I apply less force. Smooth scroll supplied by Logitech Options+ is also nice. Makes it feel like scrolling has inertia. There a lot of very nice features in Logitech Options+ like Logitech Flow Read more

review_1:
Look, I've been using computers since the early '80s. Yes, I started on an IBM 8086 and learned to type on one of those old, clunky, off-white, monster keyboards. If your over 40, you know exactly which ones I'm talking about. The thing is, I really like those old, noisy, clunky keys. I knew the moment I pressed a key, that I had actually pressed the key. I just don't get that tactile feedback I enjoy, from these newer, rubber plunger type keyboards. With my getting up in age and less and less feeling in my fingertips, I really need that tactile feedback to let me know, I'm actually typing, not just tapping on my desk with no results.

So, I like these gaming keyboards. Problem is, I've usually had to pay well over $100 to get one of any quality. And, with my coffee, tea, water, and CATS, the keyboards usually end up dying in less than a year. Ouch.

I really like this keyboard. It has really nice tactile feedback. The key does make a soft 'click' when tapped, but not that annoyingly LOUD tick.tick..ticktick..tick.. of the old IBM Model M keyboards. Anyhoot, I like the soft tick sound and the tactile feedback, to let me know I am actually depressing the intended keys, without having to constantly look up at my screen to double-check (ok, I still have to look up, because I still make a lot of typos). I also like the lighted keyboard, with the key between the right side Fn and CTRL keys to turn the keyboard lights on and off. I get up early, usually around 3-4 am. I have my LED desk lamp, but that doesn't light up the keyboard tray of my desk. Being able to turn on the keyboard light, to see the keys, early in the morning is really helpful. Then, once daylight arrives, I can easily turn off the keyboard lights, so as not to have the rainbow of colors staring back at me all day.

Yes, for the price, I think this is an INCREDIBLE keyboard, for those who like the soft tick and tactile feedback of the keyboards of yore. As for gaming? I'll let you read some young gamer's review. I'm not that guy, well, except a little solitaire. Yah, this keyboard works great for that. ;-)

review_2:

So, I thought I should go back to the USB mouse and keyboard for quick response devices. I like something with backlight LED and I came across this product on amazon. There are numerous out there, but this one has the best price as I could find within a short span of time, 30 minutes.

The keyboard has 5 levels of LED brightness and two modes of lighting: stayed-on and breathing. For the level of brightness, press and hold the sun-like key at the lower right corner and press Page-Up or Page-Down to go through the 5 levels of brightness. To switch between two modes of lighting, press and hold the Function key and press the sun-like key to toggle between the two modes. To turn off/on the LED backlight, press the sun-like key. The build of the keyboard is fine. I'm not using it for playing games so I don't know how it would work in a gaming environment. But for typing job, it does great. It is pretty quiet and responsive. I have never typed a button twice a letter. My keyboard does have a problem with the Enter key, though. It's kind of stuck and if I hit it with the same torque I use to type other keys during typing, it will not go down. I have to hit it again with higher torque ;) ... but I can live with that. All other functions that you would need, such as volume adjustment, playing music, check email, home button, calculator, and so on are just the matter of pressing the Function key with the F(s) keys. The seller claims that you can take off the keycaps to clean the keyboards. I have not tried it because I don't want to break mine.

The mouse has seven LED light colors. You cannot change between these. It changes itself. There are six buttons on the mouse: left-click, right-click, the scrolling wheel, a button-on-the -fly to change the DPI (dots per inch) between 1200/1600/2400/3200 values, and two buttons on the left side of the mouse (I use these two buttons mostly to go back or forward when I browsing the websites). The mouse is OPTICAL, not laser. It is probably because they really mean this mouse for playing games. The Mouse is not thick and is quite small. If you have a big hand, you may not like it.

The worst thing about this product is the manual. It is the most terrible manual I have ever seen. It just tells you the specs numbers and what the Function key does when being use with F1, F2, F3 and so on.

I would buy this product again and would recommend this product.

review_1: This is the second Logitech MK850 keyboard and mouse combo set I have purchased. The first one worked great until I spilled a drink on it. review_2: Had the MX series for .. well .. ever, until the mouse clicker started misbehaving - that and I had to use a USB switcher to switch between work and home computers (I work from home). This guy .. now this guy is perfect. The 1-2-3 button on the keyboard and mouse, which are independent from each other, are fantastic. At first I thought it was annoying - why on earth would I want my mouse on one computer and my keyboard on the other -- ohh, but I DO I DO ... kick off a play list/netflix/something on my personal while merrily writing up a doc on work. It's great!!My biggest suggestion is to NOT use bluetooth. I think it sucks too much battery, and is much slower to connect, and often - especially with Mac - doesn't always make the connection. My work computer has a pre-boot password (bit-locker thing) so can't use bluetooth with it. With the universal USB - it's INSTANT workie workie happie happie go go go. Works pre-boot every time, and I'm convinced it uses less battery as well.Even tho the keyboard is louder -- not quite old IBM bashie bashie keyboard loud, but maybe close -- it FEELS GOOD. It's nice and responsive. Not soft and squishy did I press the key at all? The mouse is not as big as the MX850 (I think that's what I had) - but it's a good size, feels nice in my average girl sized hand. The device switcher button on the mouse does not get in the way of normal use.The feature I do not use is Flow. Flow is this handy-dandy-feature that allows you to mouse over to the side of your screen and it'll auto switch (I think just the mouse) to the other computer). In theory it seems nice - but I think my setup confuses it. I have a Mac and a PC and both of them share a monitor - during work hours my work laptop uses it, then off hours I manually switch the monitor (using monitor menu) to my mac -- so trying to use flow it sorta gets lost on the mac and I can't get it to switch back - probably because it can't actually get to that side of the screen. But, it's really not a must have feature to me. I'm too controlly that way.I like that the keyboard has both windows, mac, laptop labels on the buttons .. example: one button has start/alt/opt, another has alt/cmd/apple .. has the fn keys too. Makes using it very handy for my apple handicapped hubby. Because it has laptop fn keys some standard keystrokes need modifcations, but it's easy ... like print screen is fn+insert (has camera icon) .. and limited print screen is ctrl+fn+insert .. but they're all close so easy -- little tweaks in the day of the life.Have I mentioned I really do like this keyboard/mouse? yes, yes I do. you might too. :)All in all two hearty thumbs up. Really great replacement for my previous Logitech, I didn't think it could get better - and this is definitely better. Read more

review_1: I purchased this, “Keyboard and Mouse Combo” off Amazon about 2 years ago. My current keyboard at the time had just been broken because the cord and plug on the keyboard had been damaged. I was also redecorating my room at the time and wanted a bit more of a “modern” keyboard for my desktop, as I am always using my desktop for something, whether it be homework, Netflix, etc. After receiving the combo-pack, I was surprised at how easy it was to operate and the convenience of not having cords all over my desk. You simply have to insert the dongle from the keyboard and mouse into your computer, power on the keyboard and mouse, and that is it! The durability is also extremely good. I have typed paper after paper for my college classes these past two years and both still function just as well as the day I got them. In fact, they are what I am using to write this review currently! This combo also provides accessible comfort, as they automatically connect to your computer as soon as you power them on, you can use the keyboard and mouse in your lap, on your bed, in your favorite comfortable chair, etc. One downside about having a wireless keyboard and mouse is that they operate off of batteries. So, I do have to go out and purchase batteries occasionally, although, as I said I am always using my desktop, typing papers for school, etc. and I usually only have to grab some new batteries every couple of months. Overall, this product is convenient, accessible, extremely durable, long-lasting, and definitely worth the price tag of $35 for the number of years it will last you, and the accessibility it will give to you. I would recommend this keyboard and mouse combo to anyone who uses their computer a lot and would appreciate not having to deal with the traditional worry of cords being damaged, pulled, or yanked, or the foot worth of cord from your keyboard and mouse that chains you to the confines of your desk. review_2: The mouse is a little smaller than I had anticipated, but going from a full size to a more travel size hasn't been an issue. It still fits well enough in my hand, and it works splendidly, even with my old computer. I needed a new set when my old Logitech bluetooth finally gave out, and decided to stick with the brand that works.I'm glad my loyalty was rewarded! Logitech has stepped up their game since my last keyboard set. Now I can easily see when the keyboard is on or off, rather than having to pick it up and look for the tiny switch hidden away underneath. There's a visible light for caps lock, so I don't give someone a surprise through a quickly typed and entered instant message.Better yet, there's a whole row of interesting buttons at the top. Granted, I won't use quite a bit of them, but having access to the volume and power functions of my computer in a very out-of-the way place makes it much easier. I usually plug my laptop into a projector for movie nights, and it can be a pain to get up, find the laptop in the dark, and putter around with finding the next movie. Having a keyboard and mouse set that's not wired in means I can be anywhere in my living room and won't have to get up in between films. And if I just so happen to decide to just sleep on the couch, I still won't have to get up to turn off the computer. But, since the buttons are on a dedicated row fully separated from the rest of the keys, it severely limits the chance of you accidentally hitting a button you didn't want.The mouse is extremely responsive (too much at times, personally), but the pointer speed can easily be fixed. There are some drivers that are recommended to download, and I say download whichever ones you find. The ones that automatically downloaded when I plugged in the keyboard were well enough, and I could still do everything I needed to with this product, but the accessory driver on Logitech's website gave a nice interface for me to interact with the keyboard and mouse. With that I was able to play around with a couple of personalizations I didn't even know I could do, and this keyboard is more attuned to my needs.If you're looking for a blend of quality and price, Logitech's lower level keyboards are definitely the way to go. Unless you're a big gamer, or use the keyboard extensively, there's not much of a need to upgrade from this product. Read more

review_2:
I'm loving this keyboard! I'm having trouble deciding whether to call it "full-size" or not. On my desktop keyboard, the keys measure 11" across. On the TeckNet wireless keyboard, the keys measure 10.75" across. So for my purposes, it is a full-size keyboard. As such, I have had no adjustment period with this keyboard. Of course, they key travel isn't the same as a desktop keyboard. But if you have every used an ultrabook keyboard, then this will feel instantly familiar. The keyboard is light, but the rubber feet on the back keep it stable on your desk/table while typing.

The keyboard uses a USB receiver which connected and worked flawlessly. The USB receiver stores in the battery compartment on the back of the unit. Two AAA batteries power the keyboard and there is an ON/OFF switch on the back. The function key row also doubles as the media keys, Home, Search, etc. Funny side note - I just tried the alternate function for the F10 key. There is a power symbol (that would be PC power, not Black Power) on the key and I expected a window to pop up giving me power down choices. But instead it just instantly put my PC to sleep. I was kind of freaking out because I thought it had shut down and I had lost all my work. But it was just sleeping.

I haven't used the keyboard long enough to honestly evaluate the battery life. The company says up to 6 months on the battery and they say it has a smart sleep mode to conserve battery for those times that you forget to turn the switch to off. There is also a low power indication on the keyboard - the caps lock light will change to red and flash when it is time to change the batteries.

All-in-all this is a great little keyboard at a great price.

review_1:
This keyboard is amazing in so many ways. It's performance is impeccable and the build and LED quality is top notch. I switched this out from my K558 Rainbow keyboard because I wanted to try out a Full RGB one and needed more space on my desk. This keyboard was a perfect choice.

Typing on it is very satisfying and responsive. Also, I am using it without a palm rest of any sort and it is still very comfortable to type on. This keyboard clearly doesn't come with a palm rest as it is part of the design.

Aesthetically, this keyboard is awesome too. It's nothing super flashy. The brushed metal is a lot more darker in person. It is noticeable, just not silver or dark gray, but closer to a black brushed metal, which I personally like a lot more anyways. The coolest thing I like about the build itself is that there is no red plastic on the keyboard anywhere. This means that anyone can use this keyboard regardless of the work station or gaming build color scheme. This is a huge plus to a lot of people who want to use the awesome products Redragon makes but choose not to because of the forced red hard plastic that is found on many other models.

The RGB lighting itself is also amazing. There is no software needed to use it either. It is all ready to go out of box with about 18 different color effect modes along with stationary colors. The lighting has no on/off feature, but it can be 'disabled' by just turning down the brightness till they are off which is good anyways since it just saves an unnecessary separate command for doing that. The animations are extremely smooth and satisfying and the RGB appears to have a full range of colors (although for solid colors, you are limited to 8 since there is no fine tuning software). You can also change the speed of animations using Fn+'- or +' keys and you change the direction of certain animations using Fn+'left arrow'. The color modes are changed using Fn+'Ins, Home, PgUp, Del, End, PgDn'. Each one has 3 different modes.

Now with every product, there is always some sort of flaw, with this keyboard, I found that there is no way to custom map which keys stay lit. Unlike my K558 where I can select individual keys to stay on and quickly swap between setups for different games, this keyboard only allows animations or solid colors across the full board. Being able to do something like set up my WASD to light up one color and have my number keys be a different color would have been nice, but it is a feature I won't use anyways since that would defeat the purpose of having a full RGB keyboard.

My final verdict is that this keyboard is an absolute steal. The price is very fair and affordable and the build and lighting quality is extremely impressive. It will fit any build design and looks beautiful as is. Plus the mechanical keys are just so fun to type on. If you need a new keyboard, this is the one you should get.

Blue mechanical switches are very clicky. I personally like the feel and sound of it. They are hot swappable and it includes a metal switch puller plus 3 pieces extra blue switches.

The RGB comes with onboard RGB presets and is FULLY CUSTOMIZABLE using a SOFTWARE. RGB direction, speed and brightness can also be controlled onboard. Brightness is enough, not too bright that it would cause a distraction.

TKL (tenkeyless) form factor, is a plus for me since it gives me extra space on my desk. A good choice for those who have tight areas to work on, or those who are travelling a lot and want to bring a keyboard. Also has onboard multimedia functions and RGB controls.

Macros and RGB can be edited using software. Yes, there is a software. Don't believe others saying there isn't. Most Redragon keyboards and mice have a dedicated software. And YES the MACROS work! You can use ANY KEY for any keyboard/multimedia macro function.

Support is TOPNOTCH. That is all I can say.

I have a Redragon mouse and I love it, but was skeptical in spending money for their keyboard (although they're already priced low). I am glad I made the leap! review_2:
I was shipped a different version of trigger stick than shown. The handle and placement of the topfire button are different than in the photos; the one I received has a centered topfire button whereas the product photos show a button angled to the rear.

There is a lot of rotational slop in the handle and shaft - the shaft is keyed into a diecast pivot (which is nice), but the mechanical tolerances between the keyway in the pivot and the mating flange on the shaft allowed for about 10 degrees of very loose clockwise and counterclockwise rotation of the handle. I shimmed the shaft-to-pivot clearance and that has reduced the rotation and looseness by about half, but not eliminated it as there is also a loose tolerance between the diecast pivot and the receiver it fits into on the outside diameter.

The handle shell is very lightweight and cheap-feeling, and the switches for the triggers do not have very pleasant action - they can be improved by removing the spring from the switch for the topfire button and 'tuning' the tightness of the two screws holding the upper portion of the handle together.

The stick is fairly softly sprung with a square restrictor, which in and of itself is not necessarily a bad thing. I do think that adding some mass inside the handle and fitting a stiffer spring to compensate for inertia will improve the overall feel and sense of solidity. There are not many choices for arcade-style topfire trigger sticks out there, and I think that this one can be made to do the job, but if you choose this one, plan on exercising your hardware and mechanical skills to get it the rest of the way there.

There is a lot to like about the AJ099, coming in at around $25 at the time of my review. It features a good shape, lightweight build and decent specs. The sensor is a budget sensor, but it doesn't feel bad in my usage. It uses Huano blue shell white dot switches, which feel very consistent, high quality, and are surprisingly spammable. The implementation is better than Zowie mice that use these same switches, IMO. The scroll wheel uses a TTC encoder and is performing fine in my testing. The mouse wheel steps are well-defined and fairly smooth. There is some occasional noise, however. The middle click is fairly stiff and not spammable. The side buttons are oddly placed/positioned and require a lot of pressure. It isn't as easy to roll my thumb upward to activate them as it is in other mice. The mouse feet are fairly poor, even after removing the plastic film. Moving it up and down causes it to drag, whereas side to side is relatively smooth. The base of the mouse also does not seem to be very even and the mouse rocks from side to side easily. There is some occasional shell flex/creaking but no rattling sounds. Nothing very noticeable while in game or wearing headphones, though. The software works well and allows you to adjust the DPI in increments of 50. You can also enable smoothing and angle snapping if you so desire. There is an option called "Peak Performance", but I am unsure what it does. There is a drop-down for LOD but it seems to be stuck at 1mm. Overall, if you are on a budget this is a pretty good option if you want something wireless and lightweight. It is considerably lighter than something like the G305, and offers rechargeability with the included rubber USB-C cable. It seems like they tried to cut corners with this mouse, unlike the AJ199 I have previously tried, but for the price I feel like it is hard to do better.

It's the kind of scent that turns heads, but in the most understated and classy way.

To top it off, La Vie Est Belle doesn’t just smell incredible; it evokes a sense of joy and optimism. The name itself, which translates to "life is beautiful," perfectly captures the essence of this fragrance. It’s a celebration of life, love, and all the little moments that make life feel special.

If you're considering investing in a high-quality perfume, I highly recommend Lancôme La Vie Est Belle Eau de Parfum. If you're looking for a fragrance that exudes sophistication, freshness, and a touch of luxury, Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone is the perfect choice. This unisex Eau de Parfum (EDP) is a true masterpiece, especially for men who want a scent that captivates while remaining elegant and timeless. Milestone carries the spirit of Creed, offering a fragrance that feels exclusive and refined, yet accessible.

From the opening, Milestone delivers a burst of fresh citrus notes: bergamot, lemon, and a splash of grapefruit. This invigorating start creates a sense of confidence and vitality, making it ideal for daily wear, whether for casual outings or professional settings. The top notes are bright but not overpowering, making it versatile for a variety of occasions.

As the fragrance evolves, the heart reveals a delightful blend of floral and herbal notes, gently softening the initial citrus blast. A smooth, clean vibe emerges with hints of rose and lavender, balanced with underlying green accords, creating a fresh, almost aquatic quality. This middle phase feels refined and sophisticated, developing into something more complex over time.

However, the true magic of Milestone shines through in its base, leaving a lasting impression of warm, woody undertones mixed with a soft musk. Notes of sandalwood, oakmoss, and amber provide a grounded depth that lingers on the skin, giving it a polished, mature finish. The longevity is impressive, lasting about 8 hours on the skin and all day if applied to clothing.

What really sets Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone apart is how it captures the essence of luxury fragrances like Creed, particularly Creed Aventus, with its fresh, masculine elegance. While it has its own unique twist, the spirit of that sophisticated luxury is unmistakable in Milestone. As the fragrance develops, it becomes more intriguing and mysterious, with an irresistible woody aroma emerging about an hour after application on the skin. This transformation turns the scent into something truly captivating.

Though Milestone is marketed as unisex, it leans slightly more masculine, making it a great choice for men who appreciate a fresh, clean, and refined fragrance. Its performance is outstanding, with a noticeable sillage that isn't overpowering but lasts throughout the day.

Manufactured in Dubai, Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone delivers the quality and craftsmanship that the region is known for, offering a high-end fragrance experience at an affordable price.

In summary, Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone is an impressive fragrance that combines freshness with complexity in a way few others can. It's perfect for those looking for a scent that’s energetic yet sophisticated, ideal for any occasion. The 3.6 oz bottle provides excellent value, ensuring you’ll enjoy this exceptional fragrance for months to come. Whether you're new to the Armaf brand or a long-time fan, Milestone is sure to impress. With its essence evoking the spirit of Creed, it’s a luxury scent without the hefty price tag.

review_1:
I'm a pretty enthusiastic collector of fragrances. I buy one for my wife now and then but she's not tremendously adventurous with fragrances and has ended up ignoring about a dozen I've given her in favor of one of the very first I bought her, a long time ago, D&G Light Blue. It's a pleasant but thoroughly unexceptional fragrance.

Well, I recently got her Kenzo D'Ete and that sort of sparked something. I guess I'd done a poor job selecting. She likes that one. Kenzo, Issey Miyake and Success de Paris are some of my own favorites, bar none (including my various high-end bottles from Amouage, L'Artisan Parfumeur, Le Labo, Montale and so on). She liked the Kenzo Summer. So I picked up Kenzo Flower. She likes it a great deal... and I have to admit, I LOVE it. I think this fragrance is going to put a new spark in our marriage because a woman smelling like this... yum. Yum yum, scrumptious!

Ok, aside from waxing poetic (and failing, miserably so in fact), the fragrance itself: I can't speak to top/mid/base note differences. But I can speak to the base note. It's a syrupy flower. Flower syrup. It's in the same vein as Kenzo Power for men... it's a kung-pow punch to your nose of impossibly pleasant flowery serum. It's sweet but not cloying, so when I say "flower syrup" I mean something more like a finely crafted attar. It has a clear, bright, 'watery' rose note very similar to Le Labo Rose 31, but there's iris, chrysanthemum. My wife thought it was powdery but she says that about every floral scent, and to my nose, it's not the least powdery. It has a perfectly reasonable balance of ambergris. So it's sweet, but not cloying. It's appropriate, and the sweetness is a background to this one-two knockout punch of delightful and just... ugh... sexy bouquet.

OK, I'm sold. I think she likes it a great deal, and it's my new favorite for her! Our 11th anniversary is coming up and I may make a special request for this fragrance to be part of her wardrobe on our special night! :)

As a husband smelling this on his wife, I'm giving it a 5-star rating, and if I could give it 6, I would. I speak for no one but myself, but for a household with many hundreds of fragrances in circulation, for a new one to have THIS distinctive and impressive impact really kind of stands for itself. Consider yourself... warned? Informed? Encouraged? Well whatever it is. Get yourself (or your spouse) one if romance is in the air. They've bottled it here. :)

Overall, if you want another cherry to add to your collection, especially one that's very different from the current offerings, give Dazzle a try. I really think you'll be happy you did.

description: Fancy by Jessica Simpson for Women bottle holds 3.4 ounce EDP Spray | It includes pear, apricot, red berries, gardenia, jasmine, almond , caramel, sandalwood, vanilla and amber
review_1:
I sold my 20+ bottles of high-end eau de parfums many, many years ago when my migraines no longer allowed me to wear fragrances of any kind. I recently discovered (accidentally) that I can wear perfume again without getting an immediate headache but only certain scents like vanilla-based gourmands or light fruit-based scents. After wearing Marc Jacobs' "Daisy Eau So Fresh" successfully all summer, I was looking for a warm vanilla/caramel type scent for autumn/winter. I was surprised by how many YouTube perfume snobs recommended this Jessica Simpson fragrance and at under $20 for a 3.4 oz bottle of "Fancy", it was a blind-buy no-brainer. Well, the YouTubers were right. It is a lovely, well-rounded, perfect for cooler weather, inviting fragrance that works well for daytime or evening. The dry-down is exactly a nice creamy, caramel vanilla vibe that lasts surprisingly long and doesn't ever smell artificial or cheap. I get a solid 8 hours from this fragrance with one spray to each wrist and one to my neck. The sillage really only lasts the first 2-3 hours which is just fine with me. I like more intimate fragrances anyway. I prefer to share my scents with only those closest to me, and speaking of those closest, my husband loves this one. Whether you're a picky perfumery expert or just someone looking for an affordable workhorse of a winter fragrance, you cannot go wrong with this yummy gourmand. I rarely gift fragrances but I would definitely give this to any perfume lover/collector unless they specifically have a dislike of gourmand scents. The packaging and bottle are very attractive too. "Fancy" really holds its own among even high-end designer eau de parfums. Ms. Simpson should be very proud of her contribution to the fragrance world.

review_1:
I had completely forgotten I had pre-ordered this fragrance. I couldn't remember the scent notes or had any idea what it was supposed to smell like. There was a smooth creaminess, a hint of espresso/coffee or cocoa(hard to differentiate), and the jasmine. As for strength and lasting power: The strength is about the same as the other Sabrina Carpenter perfumes. It is moderately strong when sprayed, but loses power after about an hour. The dry down after an hour is mostly a sweet, creamy jasmine. It is gorgeously feminine and can be worn any time, day or night, any season. The lasting power is fair--4 to 6 hours on me. However, it's projection weakens over that entire time. I am pleasantly surprised that I love this scent so much, as it is completely different from what I had expected. Up until this point, Sweet Tooth Caramel(beige bottle), was my favorite. Me Espresso may have just kicked it out of the number one spot. I highly recommend this perfume. review_1:
I always wanted to see the hype behind this scent. Believe me when I say this is one of the best scent you can buy. I have a big collection of designer, niche, and cheap fragrance. This is one which I go for the most for my daily use. The sweet vanilla with a little smoky touch is just so right!!! The starting is a little smoky and vanilla. The dry down is a lot more calm and sweet. Reminds me of stronger with you line. Very well done, clean scent especially for the winter or fall.

The quality feels great unlike many other cheap brands. Lasts for a long time. I can smell this on my skin after 8 to 10 hours easily. So performance is top notch. Another thing that is so good is the presentation. Starting from the box to the actual bottle, it is no less than a designer.
review_2:
This is a gorgeous, sweet and spicy fragrance! Khamrah Dukhan opens with a burst of sweetness, and you immediately get the spices. The pimento pepper is hot in a way that tingles the nose. It also feels hot to the touch. I accidentally touched my lips to the paper when I went to smell it, and it did cause them to sting a little bit. But it smells incredible. The sweetness from the original Khamrah DNA is there: the syrupy and potent date/praline/vanilla/caramel blend— though it’s mild when you first spray it, letting the spices truly shine.

As the fragrance settles on skin, the sweetness intensifies. I get a rich, ambery, syrupy scent, with caramel undertones and wafts of cinnamon sugar. To some, the syrupy-sweet scent can almost even smell honey-like, though there’s no natural honey smell in this fragrance. The cinnamon and pimento stay noticeable throughout the entire wear of the perfume; and there’s a mild leathery nuance that’s in the background. It’s well blended, and not very noticeable. Overall, this is a gorgeous, decadent sweet and spicy bomb of a fragrance!

In my opinion, this is truly unisex and doesn’t lean either masculine or feminine. Anyone who enjoys the Khamrah line’s DNA, and also likes spices in fragrances, will very likely love this. Some women may think it leans masculine because of the pimento and subtle leather, and some men may find it too sweet— it really just comes down to preference. However, as a woman who loves spicy fragrances and absolutely loves sweet scents, this is incredible!

On my skin, I get at least 10 hours of wear out of this perfume, with about two hours of good projection. It takes hours before I feel it sits close to the skin. If you want more projection, I’d spray this in clothing. I sprayed this on a paper towel, and could smell it through the air every time I walked past my dining room table, where I’d set it down. It’s pretty potent. Sillage is excellent, and if oversprayed this could definitely be cloying or even a room filler. I would definitely let this one sit at least a day before making judgements, however. When I first got it, the scent was stilted because it was delivered in negative degree weather. Within a day, it was settled, strong, and ready for a good wear. The bottle is thick, sturdy, and has an excellent, misty atomizer, with no leaks. And you get 100mls of perfume for less than $30.

10/10 for the scent, performance, and amount you get for the price!

review_1:
I NEVER write reviews, but I figured my review might help for some who might have questions.

1. This perfume seems REAL it just comes in an ugly tester box instead of pretty packaging. What’s a tester box you ask? Well, it’s a plain cardboard box. I worked in the perfume business for awhile and a tester box saves the wholesale buyer some money on packaging. The perfume is not used…it just saves the business some money since it is assumed they are going to place that particular bottle on the shelf to be “tested” and throw the packing away. You can buy “tester” versions of pretty much any fragrance and it’ll save you some money. I recommend keeping your lids though, because SOMETIMES some testers do NOT come with a lid. This Britney Spears one DOES come with a lid though!
2. Elizabeth Arden is the fragrance company who partnered with Britney Spears to create the fragrance. Hence her name being on there. I mean, people don’t just have fragrance/cosmetic labs in their homes right? Britney had to partner with someone!
3. If you’re gifting this…I might not buy it. Unless you’re okay with taking it out of the ugly cardboard box and putting it in cellophane with a pretty ribbon or something.

In all, this fragrance seems like the real deal. Smells bomb and lasts as long as I remember. It takes me back to circa 2005! You just don’t get the “pretty box” because it’s a “tester” bottle. This was fine by me as I bought it for pure nostalgia! I rock it around the house or to the gym for a workout and it smells JUST like I remembered it smelling!

review_1:
So I bought this fragrance years ago for the first time (maybe 2021 or 2022?). I loved it from the moment I smelled it and thought it was so unique. It smelled like sunshine in a bottle to me and instantly made me feel happier! The name is very fitting for this fragrance. I used it up and went in to try other fragrances after that. Now, fast forward to 2025, I’m looking for a nice tropical/hawaiin/beachy vacation type of scent and this fragrance came to mind after so many years! I decided to order it off memory. It smells amazing in the bottle. I sprayed it for the first time in so many years and for the first 20 minutes it wasn’t my favorite - the florals really came out and it smelled a bit perfume-y for my liking (I have a sensitive nose and I like body oils usually more than perfumes so I’m just not used to perfumes. This would probably be a very light scent for strong perfume lovers). I waited for it to settle a bit and now I absolutely love it. It’s the exact scent I remember and it dries down into a lovely expensive resort spa /sunscreen scent (in a good way) with undertones of coconut and white flowers that aren’t overpowering. I am obsessed with it and I’m so glad I didn’t base my review off of the first few minutes. This scent has the potential to be your absolute favorite scent / signature scent if you allow it to. I realized that it’s ALL in the application. If you spray on your skin from close up it’s going to bring out the perfumey scent and florals more than if you MIST from afar or even spray the air and walk through it. I sprayed in my inner elbow from about 10 inches away and after about 20 minutes I love the scent. You have to allow the fragrance to settle before judging it!!! Spray 20 minutes before leaving the house and you and others will love the way you smell when you leave. In my opinion, this fragrance is worth the buy. It smells expensive and more complex than the other beachy scents out there and it’s not too strong once it settles. It’s truly a delightful scent that stays close to you and creates a nice, personal scent cloud around you without leaving a trail. The bottle is very nice. It’s much nicer than other travel size bottles / sprays that make you feel like you have the cheap version of the fragrance as you long for the expensive full size bottle. It doesn’t feel like a mini version, it feels like a little bottle. It actually seems like it’ll last a while. I’m excited to play around with application to find what I like best! Overall happy with my purchase and hopefully it’ll become my signature scent once I figure out what my favorite way to apply it is. (It’s worth the effort!!!)

review_2:
Khamrah has been hyped for years now, but is it really worth the attention? Here are some of my thoughts based on my experience with the Original Khamrah, Khamrah Qahwa, and the newest release, Dukhan. Hopefully, this helps you decide which one might suit you—or if you’d rather skip them altogether.

Original Khamrah: Personally, I didn’t enjoy this one. To me, it smells like a wax candle you'd find in a church or something from Yankee Candle (though I can’t pinpoint the exact scent). It’s extremely sweet and very boozy. This is a definite winter fragrance and while it does smell high quality, it’s just not my style. I usually avoid overly sweet scents. However, I can see the appeal—if you enjoy strong, sweet, and boozy fragrances or like that church candle vibe, you’ll probably appreciate this. For under $30, it smells far more expensive than it is. Some people compare it to Angel’s Share by Kilian, and while I don’t think they smell exactly the same, they do share a similar DNA. Both lean toward a boozy, cinnamon-heavy profile. However, the execution is different enough that I wouldn’t call Khamrah a direct dupe. If you're familiar with Angel’s Share, you’ll recognize some of the elements, but Khamrah takes its own path.

Khamrah Qahwa: This is where the magic happens. If you didn’t enjoy the Original due to its overwhelming sweetness and you like coffee notes, this is the one to try. It tones down the sweetness of the Original and introduces a smooth coffee scent that blends beautifully. That waxy candle smell is gone, replaced by something richer and more mature. It leans boozy and sophisticated—perfect for men over 30 or anyone with a more refined style. I personally enjoy Khamrah Qahwa far more than the Original in every aspect. It’s not trying to copy any niche or designer fragrance, but it stands strong on its own as a very well-blended scent. At around $25, it’s an incredible value and smells like something much more luxurious.

Dukhan: The newest release comes in at about $20 more than the others, but when I first smelled it, it immediately reminded me of the Original Khamrah. It’s like a toned-down version of the Original with a subtle hint of spice. Not drastically different, but enough to notice. It still carries that candle-like vibe, just less sweet. If the Original gave you a headache, this one might be more tolerable. It’s still boozy and sweet, but slightly more balanced. I’d say it’s a more wearable option if you're curious about the Khamrah DNA but want something less intense.

Final thoughts: Everyone’s nose is different, and we all have unique scent preferences. As a small fragrance collector with around 50 bottles, including both UAE and designer brands, my clear favorite is Khamrah Qahwa. It strikes the perfect balance of sweetness and warmth, with that standout coffee note that I absolutely love. I picked it up for $25, and it’s also available at Burlington for about $35. It’s ideal for cold weather, date nights, or any winter occasion where you want to smell refined without overspending.

If you're just looking for a safe blind buy or something more universally appealing, Khamrah Qahwa is the way to go, especially for men over 30 or those with a mature style. If you’re curious about the Original or Dukhan, I’d recommend Dukhan since it offers a similar scent but is a little more toned down. That said, I’d wait for the price to drop below $30. If you’re into very sweet, loud, boozy, and cinnamony scents, the Original might be for you.

I hope this helps you choose the right Khamrah for your collection.

description: His Confession by Lattafa Perfumes is a Oriental Woody fragrance for men | Top Notes: Mandarin, Cinnamon and Lavender | Middle Notes: Iris, Cypress, Benzoin and Mahonial | Base Notes: Vanilla, Tonka Beans, Patchouli, Cedarwood, Incense and Amber | Ideal for any occasion
review_1:
Scent Profile & Initial Impressions

His Confession opens with a noticeable burst of cinnamon, mandarin and lavender — spicy and somewhat sharp, but also fresh from the citrus-lavender top.

As it transitions, a heart of iris, benzoin, cypress and mahonial comes through — the iris particularly gives it a somewhat powdery, refined texture.

The base then lands in a rich, warm territory: vanilla, tonka bean, amber, cedarwood, patchouli and incense. The vanilla and tonka bean soften the earlier spice and give it a gourmand-woody finish.

In summary: this fragrance marries spicy top notes with a creamy/powdery heart and a warm, sweet woody base. It leans into gourmand territory while retaining some masculine woods and incense.

Performance: Longevity, Projection & Value

Longevity: Many user reviews suggest 6-10 hours of usable wear, with some reporting scent on clothes even the next day.

Projection & Sillage: Projection is moderate to above average in early wear, but not “beast mode” territory. Some users say it ends closer to skin scent in the later dry-down.

Value: Given its price point (affordable for 100 ml EDP), many feel it offers “niche-quality” at a budget-friendly price.

Final Verdict

His Confession offers great value and a pleasant, sophisticated gourmand-woody fragrance experience. For the budget, you’re getting complex notes, strong character, and good versatility.
If you enjoy fragrances with spice (cinnamon), powdery iris, vanilla/tonka sweetness and warm woods, this is a very strong contender. If you prefer purely fresh, citrusy or ultra-masculine leather scents, you might want to sample it first.

If you're looking for a fragrance that exudes sophistication, freshness, and a touch of luxury, Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone is the perfect choice. This unisex Eau de Parfum (EDP) is a true masterpiece, especially for men who want a scent that captivates while remaining elegant and timeless. Milestone carries the spirit of Creed, offering a fragrance that feels exclusive and refined, yet accessible.

From the opening, Milestone delivers a burst of fresh citrus notes: bergamot, lemon, and a splash of grapefruit. This invigorating start creates a sense of confidence and vitality, making it ideal for daily wear, whether for casual outings or professional settings. The top notes are bright but not overpowering, making it versatile for a variety of occasions.

As the fragrance evolves, the heart reveals a delightful blend of floral and herbal notes, gently softening the initial citrus blast. A smooth, clean vibe emerges with hints of rose and lavender, balanced with underlying green accords, creating a fresh, almost aquatic quality. This middle phase feels refined and sophisticated, developing into something more complex over time.

However, the true magic of Milestone shines through in its base, leaving a lasting impression of warm, woody undertones mixed with a soft musk. Notes of sandalwood, oakmoss, and amber provide a grounded depth that lingers on the skin, giving it a polished, mature finish. The longevity is impressive, lasting about 8 hours on the skin and all day if applied to clothing.

What really sets Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone apart is how it captures the essence of luxury fragrances like Creed, particularly Creed Aventus, with its fresh, masculine elegance. While it has its own unique twist, the spirit of that sophisticated luxury is unmistakable in Milestone. As the fragrance develops, it becomes more intriguing and mysterious, with an irresistible woody aroma emerging about an hour after application on the skin. This transformation turns the scent into something truly captivating.

Though Milestone is marketed as unisex, it leans slightly more masculine, making it a great choice for men who appreciate a fresh, clean, and refined fragrance. Its performance is outstanding, with a noticeable sillage that isn't overpowering but lasts throughout the day.

Manufactured in Dubai, Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone delivers the quality and craftsmanship that the region is known for, offering a high-end fragrance experience at an affordable price.

In summary, Armaf Club De Nuit Milestone is an impressive fragrance that combines freshness with complexity in a way few others can. It's perfect for those looking for a scent that’s energetic yet sophisticated, ideal for any occasion. The 3.6 oz bottle provides excellent value, ensuring you’ll enjoy this exceptional fragrance for months to come. Whether you're new to the Armaf brand or a long-time fan, Milestone is sure to impress. With its essence evoking the spirit of Creed, it’s a luxury scent without the hefty price tag.

So, even though it is lighter, and it can wear off after a while, I just add another spray or two, every so often, as needed. This, TO ME, is an acceptable trade off, and doesn't bother me that much. (I have other perfumes that are the same way, so it's not unusual to me)

review_2: This has been the weirdest fragrance experience I’ve had so far. I went from absolutely hating this perfume to loving it within a day. And now, days later— I’m kind of obsessed with it. When I first got this fragrance in the mail, I was angry. I wanted to throw it away. It smelled outdated, sharp, and very mature to me. All I could smell was rose soap, a bit of powder, and a slight animalic undertone. I washed it off immediately and sprayed several sprays of it onto a tissue to clear any stale fragrance from the tube/ introduce more air and left it for the night. I came back to it the next morning, expecting to be irritated with my purchase all over again.I sprayed it and— soap. Yet again. I decided to just leave it for a second because I was busy. As I was sitting, I started smelling something beautiful. Something very sweet, almost syrupy sweet, and floral— but the kind of floral I like. Violets, roses, tuberose and something fruity mixed in. I sniffed my wrist and it was this perfume!!To describe the scent, it has a watery, slippery/smooth rosy smell to it, like the run off from an “expensive” rose soap bar (think those fancy “French” soaps places like Marshall’s sell for around $6+). But it also smells like violet candies, airy peonies, jasmine, and it’s not listed, but I smell a bubblegummy tuberose kind of scent (possibly from the mixture of the jasmine & violet). Mixed in, I also get a sweet sparkling fruit. The fruit note is listed as peach, but it smells more like a sweet tangerine to me. All of those beautiful floral notes along with the soapy scent and sparkling fruit make this smell so pretty, and weirdly modern, though it does have a light powderiness to it from the violets. I don’t think that this smells very vintage the longer that I have it. This actually smells like a bubble bath or bath bomb that I could imagine Barbie using. It’s ultra feminine, clean, bubbly, and sweet.My mom was right there with me saying that this smelled outdated and funky when I first sprayed it. She didn’t recognize it the next time I wore it. She said that it smelled like a nice, expensive lotion. My boyfriend said it smells like soap and candy. I typically hate soapy perfumes, but I really like this one. It absolutely is strongly soapy, but the sweetness makes it enjoyable. Can be overwhelming if sprayed too much, but otherwise it’s a beautiful perfume.The bottle is also one of my favorites. It’s gaudy and the cap doesn’t stay on great, but I love the design and women around the glass. Read more

review_2: This has been the weirdest fragrance experience I’ve had so far. I went from absolutely hating this perfume to loving it within a day. And now, days later— I’m kind of obsessed with it. When I first got this fragrance in the mail, I was angry. I wanted to throw it away. It smelled outdated, sharp, and very mature to me. All I could smell was rose soap, a bit of powder, and a slight animalic undertone. I washed it off immediately and sprayed several sprays of it onto a tissue to clear any stale fragrance from the tube/ introduce more air and left it for the night. I came back to it the next morning, expecting to be irritated with my purchase all over again.I sprayed it and— soap. Yet again. I decided to just leave it for a second because I was busy. As I was sitting, I started smelling something beautiful. Something very sweet, almost syrupy sweet, and floral— but the kind of floral I like. Violets, roses, tuberose and something fruity mixed in. I sniffed my wrist and it was this perfume!!To describe the scent, it has a watery, slippery/smooth rosy smell to it, like the run off from an “expensive” rose soap bar (think those fancy “French” soaps places like Marshall’s sell for around $6+). But it also smells like violet candies, airy peonies, jasmine, and it’s not listed, but I smell a bubblegummy tuberose kind of scent (possibly from the mixture of the jasmine & violet). Mixed in, I also get a sweet sparkling fruit. The fruit note is listed as peach, but it smells more like a sweet tangerine to me. All of those beautiful floral notes along with the soapy scent and sparkling fruit make this smell so pretty, and weirdly modern, though it does have a light powderiness to it from the violets. I don’t think that this smells very vintage the longer that I have it. This actually smells like a bubble bath or bath bomb that I could imagine Barbie using. It’s ultra feminine, clean, bubbly, and sweet.My mom was right there with me saying that this smelled outdated and funky when I first sprayed it. She didn’t recognize it the next time I wore it. She said that it smelled like a nice, expensive lotion. My boyfriend said it smells like soap and candy. I typically hate soapy perfumes, but I really like this one. It absolutely is strongly soapy, but the sweetness makes it enjoyable. Can be overwhelming if sprayed too much, but otherwise it’s a beautiful perfume.The bottle is also one of my favorites. It’s gaudy and the cap doesn’t stay on great, but I love the design and women around the glass. Read more

review_1: I absolutely adore this scent. I am a (rather masculine) “classic” man and this is what I wear on an evening out and want attention from women.Yes. This is designed as a woman’s perfume, however, as a man that collects interesting fragrances, I’ll say that this is like the “behind closed doors”of fragrances. I have never once not worn this and had women instantly speak to me because I smell so damn good.I had one person describe it as (excuse the term) a “panty dropper”.When women wear it, it exudes sex.When I wear it, it exudes sex.This won’t disappoint in that department.I wouldn’t recommend this to the “average” guy (as it takes a certain look, style, and mindset to confidently pull this off), but if you’re on the cutting edge of fashion, a bit more adventurous, and (dare I say) avant-garde this smell will compliment your whole ensemble.The reactions I get wearing this are similar to the reactions I received while wearing Gautier’s “le Male” in the 90’s (before everyone started wearing it). Mind you, it is completely different than “le Male”, however the reactions it provokes are the same.Hell, I even spray this on at night so I can smell myself as I sleep.The only negative thing about this scent is that, like other people have noted, it doesn’t linger for long. It lasts longer on clothes than skin and needs to be reapplied throughout an evening.I’ve snatched up a few bottles as it’s discontinued and becoming harder to come by. Read more
review_2: Beautiful fragrance! I wear this everyday day, makes you feel pretty and lifts your spirits. Your worth it, just go for it.I'll never be without! Read more
